articles.title: Indian man awarded nearly £30,000 by UK tribunal after employer failed to provide work - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian man, Shabin Shaji, was awarded nearly £30,000 by an employment tribunal after his employer, Swan Care Solutions Ltd, failed to provide him with work for a year despite issuing him a sponsorship visa.  The tribunal found that the company withheld work from Shaji and did not pay him wages, breaching its contractual obligations and grievance procedures. The judge stated that Shaji had done everything required to start working but was left without income or employment.

A dust storm swept across Rajasthan's Churu district, causing widespread disruption and darkness.

articles.title: Dua Lipa ties the knot with Callum Turner in London, see photos | Music News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner were married in a private ceremony at Old Marylebone Town Hall in London on Sunday. The singer wore a custom white skirt suit by Schiaparelli couture, while Turner opted for a navy double-breasted Ferragamo suit.  The couple announced their engagement last year, and have been dating since 2024.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Pema Chödrön: 'Fear is a natural reaction to moving...' — life lessons on courage, self-awareness | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Pema Chödrön, an American Buddhist teacher, author, and nun, is known for her teachings on practicing peace in turbulent times. Her quote "Fear is a natural reaction to moving closer to the truth" emphasizes that fear can be a useful guide when confronting change or facing difficult truths. This message resonates with modern readers who often seek distractions from discomfort and emotional challenges. Chödrön's work encourages individuals to pause, examine their fears, and see them as potential opportunities for growth.

articles.title: Quote of the Day by Brené Brown: 'Crazy-busy is a great armor' — life lessons on burnout, rest and emotional honesty | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Brené Brown, an American researcher and author, argues that excessive busyness can function as emotional armor, shielding individuals from uncomfortable emotions and difficult truths.  Her quote "Crazy-busy is a great armor…" challenges the belief that being busy equates to success or importance in today's fast-paced culture where productivity is often viewed as a measure of personal worth. Brown emphasizes that slowing down allows for reflection and self-awareness, leading to greater clarity and deeper connections with oneself and others.  Her message encourages individuals to examine their busyness and prioritize rest and honest self-reflection over constant activity.

articles.title: Japanese Proverb of the Day: ‘When three gather, wisdom appears’; meaning and why it still matters today | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Japanese culture emphasizes collective decision-making, as evidenced by the proverb "When three gather, wisdom appears." This proverb highlights that the best thinking often arises from dialogue and exchange between individuals with diverse perspectives.  It suggests that a third voice can break through deadlock and offer new insights, leading to understanding that is unavailable to any one person alone. The proverb encourages people to seek out honest conversations and build deliberate gatherings into their lives to foster collective intelligence and wisdom.

articles.title: ‘Why Torture Yourself?’ Taapsee Pannu Calls Out Obsession With Flat Midriff, Instagram-Perfect Photos | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Taapsee Pannu, a Bollywood actress, urged women to embrace their natural body shapes and resist unrealistic beauty standards.  She highlighted that lower belly fat and water retention are not flaws but serve as protective features for the reproductive organs. Munmun Ganeriwal, her nutritionist, supported this view, emphasizing the importance of having some healthy fat and water retention in the abdominal area. Pannu encouraged women to accept their bodies and avoid excessive workouts that can lead to unhealthy body image pressures.

articles.title: Rohit Shetty Announces New Season Of ‘Khatron Ke Khiladi’ With Action-Packed Video | OdishaBytes

articles.title: ‘Right of sex workers can exist without a right to sex work: SC asks Government to make law exempting trafficked sex workers from criminal charges | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has issued a detailed plan to protect the rights of victims of commercial sexual exploitation (CSE) while acknowledging that there is no one-size-fits-all approach. The court emphasized that trafficked victims should not be prosecuted for prostitution and called upon the government to amend the Immoral Trafficking Prevention Act (ITPA) to exempt them from prosecution.  The plan also outlines procedures for police raids to rescue victims, ensuring their dignity and safety while recognizing the complex nature of CSE and the need for a comprehensive legal framework addressing all forms of exploitation.

articles.title: Mrunal Thakur on having kids: “Of course everyone wants them”— DINK debate resurfaces
articles.rephrased_article: Rutuja Walawalkar, a psychologist at Mpower, Aditya Birla Education Trust, emphasizes the importance of emotional readiness for parents. Walawalkar suggests that societal pressures can lead to decisions based on external expectations rather than personal feelings of preparedness, potentially causing stress and resentment in relationships. This highlights the importance of considering emotional readiness when making family-planning decisions.

articles.title: Leopard suffers paw injury in Thane's national park, rescued after 21-hour op - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A leopard was rescued from Mama Bhanja Hills in Thane's Yeoor Range of Sanjay Gandhi National Park after a 21-hour operation. The animal, estimated to be four to five years old, suffered severe injuries to its paws, with bones exposed, and wounds on its body and tail.  The leopard was rescued by a team from the Maharashtra State Security Corporation (MSSC), Wildlife Welfare Association (WWA), and Resqink Association for Wildlife Welfare (RAWW), who monitored the animal before tranquilizing it and transporting it to the SGNP Leopard Rescue Centre.

articles.title: Quote of the Day by American author Earl Nightingale — ‘Wherever there is danger, there lurks opportunity…’ | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Earl Nightingale, a pioneering American radio personality and motivational speaker, is known for his quote: "Wherever there is danger, there lurks opportunity; whenever there is opportunity, there lurks danger." He emphasized that danger and opportunity are inseparable aspects of life. Nightingale co-founded the Nightingale-Conant Corporation, which produced over 7,000 radio programs and became a leading producer of personal development audio programs.  He died in 1989.

This follows several other complaints regarding unhygienic or spoiled food sold through Blinkit's platform.

articles.title: Supreme Court Judge visits Bengaluru Central Prison, launches skill development and mental health initiatives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Vikram Nath, of the Supreme Court and executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NLSA), visited the Bengaluru Central Prison on Sunday to inaugurate several initiatives aimed at improving rehabilitation, skill development, and mental healthcare services for inmates.  The delegation included Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru of the Karnataka High Court and justice Anu Sivaraman, executive chairperson of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA). The initiatives include a computer lab, a de-addiction center, a Tele-MANAS facility, and a creche for children of incarcerated mothers. These programs are expected to strengthen rehabilitation efforts and enhance the overall welfare of inmates in the state's prison system.

articles.title: N. Devidas assumes charge as KILA Director General - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Devidas, a 2015-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre, has assumed his role as Director General of the Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA).  He was welcomed by KILA staff under the leadership of Registrar K.R. Sumesh.  Devidas previously served as District Collector of Kollam and held various positions in government including Director of Mining and Geology, Managing Director of the State Backward Classes Development Corporation, Housing Commissioner, Secretary of the Housing Board, and Director of the Backward Classes Development department.

articles.title: Ajith Kumar pays last respects to mother Mohini Mani thanks Chennai police for support - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Ajith Kumar bid farewell to his mother, Mohini Mani, at a private cremation in Chennai. The actor expressed gratitude to the Chennai Police for their support during the funeral arrangements.  Family members and several members of the film fraternity offered condolences following her death on Saturday at age 85. Vijay, Trisha Krishnan, Kamal Haasan, and Radhika Sarathkumar were among those who visited Ajith's residence to offer their sympathies. The family described Mohini Mani as "the heart of our family" and said her values would continue to guide them.

articles.title: Indian woman caught shoplifting in Japan, tries to settle matter with cash - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian woman on a group tour in Japan was caught shoplifting at a souvenir store and attempted to settle the matter with money twice, first with the shopkeeper and then again at the police station. The incident sparked online discussion about tourist behavior abroad, with some users expressing embarrassment and frustration over the alleged actions while others praised the shopkeeper's restraint and the police's intervention.  The woman was ultimately warned by authorities.

articles.title: Several Kanpur BEd aspirants fall into drain after slab caves in - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Kanpur police are investigating a Sunday incident where a dilapidated concrete slab collapsed outside an examination centre, causing over 20 BEd candidates and their family members to fall into a sewage drain. The accident occurred near HN Mishra PG College as candidates gathered for the Uttar Pradesh BEd Joint Entrance Examination.  The incident sparked protests from candidates and parents who alleged negligence by civic authorities. Despite the disruption, all candidates successfully reached their examination centres.

articles.title: Watch: Meteor explodes into blinding lights over New England, loud boom jolts states - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A rare daytime bolide, or exceptionally luminous meteor, exploded over New England on May 30th, causing sonic booms felt as far away as Montreal. NASA confirmed the object was a natural meteoroid, measuring approximately one meter in diameter and traveling at 75,000 miles per hour when it collided with Earth's atmosphere. The event caused widespread shockwaves but did not result in any injuries or damage.  The sonic boom was detected by satellites from NOAA and the ground shaking was attributed to atmospheric pressure waves.

articles.title: Video: Monkey’s ‘money rain’ leaves UP crowd scrambling for notes - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A monkey in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, stole a bag containing Rs 2 lakh from a man near the district court complex. The monkey then climbed a tree and began scattering the currency notes from the bag, creating a spectacle that drew a crowd of onlookers.  The owner of the bag raised an alarm, and locals helped recover nearly Rs 1.98 lakh of the lost money.

articles.title: Madhuri Dixit Fires Back At Trolls Over Aishwarya Rai’s Cannes Appearances | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Aishwarya Rai Bachchan faced online criticism for her appearance at the 2026 Cannes red carpet, prompting support from Madhuri Dixit.  Dixit defended Rai Bachchan, stating that she is a global star who has achieved much for India and should not be judged by superficial standards. Other actors, including Triptii Dimri, also expressed concern about the negative comments directed at them online, emphasizing the importance of respecting achievements over physical appearance. They believe social media has amplified this negativity, creating an environment where people feel empowered to comment on others' work without considering their efforts and dedication.

articles.title: Mahendra Purushottam Mela & Maha Yajna: Odisha’s Mahendragiri Ready For 9-Day Spiritual Extravaganza | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Commerce and Transport Minister Bibhuti Bhushan Jena reviewed preparations for the nine-day Mahendra Purushottam Mela and Maha Yajna at the Mahendragiri hill shrine, which is expected to host nearly 3 lakh devotees. The event will feature religious rituals, cultural programs, and devotional activities from June 1st to 9th.  Extensive facilities have been arranged for accommodation, drinking water, sanitation, healthcare, and transportation. This is the first time a Maha Yajna and mela are being held at Mahendragiri during Purushottam Maas, making it a special occasion for devotees.

articles.title: Huge fire destroys two units in an automobile factory in Sriperumbudur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out in the waste storage area of a Hyundai Mobis factory in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu on Sunday. The blaze quickly spread throughout the facility, creating thick black smoke that was visible from the Chennai-Bengaluru highway. Hyundai Mobis officials evacuated all workers and called emergency services. Firefighters battled the fire for over four hours before bringing it under control. Two factory units were completely destroyed in the incident.

articles.title: ‘Everything Shown Was True’: Ex-Karachi Mayor Supports 'Dhurandhar' Amid Lyari Debate | OdishaBytes

The 'Dhurandhar' franchise, directed by Aditya Dhar, is set against the backdrop of Karachi's Lyari neighborhood, which plays a significant role in the espionage story. The sequel, 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge', expands on the scale of the conflict and follows Hamza Ali Mazari, played by Ranveer Singh, as he delves deeper into the region's criminal landscape.

articles.title: Huge fire destroys two units in an automobile factory in Sriperumbudur - The Hindu

Hyundai Mobis officials alerted authorities, who dispatched fire tenders and rescue personnel from both Sriperumbudur and Oragadam stations. After four hours of fighting the fire, it was brought under control, resulting in the destruction of two factory units.

articles.title: Gulmarg Gondola remains suspended, no timeline yet for resumption
articles.rephrased_article: Syed Qamar Sajjad, Managing Director of the Gulmarg Gondola Project, stated that no decision has been made on resuming operations following a technical fault that suspended service since May 25.  The Gulmarg Gondola will begin refunding tourists who booked tickets between May 25 and June 2 or 3. All passengers were safely evacuated during the incident, with no injuries reported. The authorities have not yet announced a timeline for restoring the service.

articles.title: Fresh Backlash Against ISKCON Over 'Untimely' Baltimore Rath Yatra | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: ISKCON chapters in Baltimore defied traditional practices by holding their annual Rath Yatra on May 30th, sparking global outrage from devotees and the Odia diaspora.  The decision to hold the festival outside of the prescribed Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya date has been criticized as arbitrary and disrespectful to religious traditions. Devotees argue that altering the sacred timeline undermines the spiritual sanctity of the event. ISKCON has given written assurances about adhering to traditional schedules in India, but continues to bypass these rules overseas.  The Srimandir managing committee has previously appealed to government officials for intervention against these scriptural deviations.

articles.title: PM Modi urges people to take precautions amid scorching heat
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to stay hydrated during the ongoing heatwave across India.  He emphasized taking precautions when stepping outside and following government guidelines on hydration. Modi also highlighted the importance of mangoes, noting their regional variations and global reach.

articles.rephrased_article: Harsh Goenka, chairman of RPG Group, criticized India's civic sense, citing incidents like garba performances at airports and loud music in public spaces. Goenka also shared a set of rules displayed at a Swiss hotel specifically for Indian guests, which he found appalling. These guidelines included restrictions on food removal from the breakfast buffet and noise levels. The controversy sparked online discussions with some users highlighting examples of poor civic sense in India while others urged for improvement.

The impact of these projects extended beyond Malayalam cinema and even impacted the Telugu and Tamil markets.

articles.title: From a ‘Cheetah’ Chief to Cheetah squadron: Why Army Chief has special wishes for the Champion squadron at NDA | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: General Upendra Dwivedi, the Army Chief, congratulated the Charlie Squadron of the National Defence Academy (NDA) on winning the coveted Chiefs of Staff Banner at their 150th Passing Out Parade.  The banner signifies excellence in training, academics, and overall performance over the entire term.  Dwivedi, an alumnus of the Charlie squadron himself, expressed his admiration for the squadron's achievements and shared memories of his time as a cadet. The winning squadron will display the banner atop its building and mount ceremonial guns at the entrance for the next term.

articles.title: Gurgaon's AC auto is the summer upgrade commuters didn't know they needed - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A Gurgaon auto rickshaw fitted with a working air conditioner has gone viral on Instagram, capturing the attention of social media users. The clip shows the vehicle cruising through the city, offering a glimpse into a more comfortable commute for passengers during India's intense summer heat. Many online viewers expressed surprise and admiration for the innovation, while some questioned why other auto drivers haven't adopted similar modifications.

articles.title: Pranit More under fire for Peak Gurgaon content Uorfi Javed reacts - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Pranit More, a comedian who gained fame on Bigg Boss 19, has come under fire for a viral stand-up clip where he laughed at an audience member's crude date story. The video, which was shared by content creator Uorfi Javed, sparked criticism online, with users calling his response "peak rapist content" and accusing him of normalizing sexual harassment. While the clip has been deleted from More's account, social media users continue to condemn his actions, highlighting the harmful implications of such humor.

articles.title: AI Solves 80-Year-Old Math Problem That Stumped Experts For Decades
articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI's advanced AI model has disproven a long-standing mathematical conjecture by Paul Erdos, solving the unit distance problem. The AI found counterexamples that showed the maximum number of pairs of points exactly one unit apart could exceed previously expected bounds. This breakthrough in combinatorial geometry is considered a significant milestone in AI mathematics and highlights the potential for AI to contribute original scientific research.

articles.title: Media burnout, career break and sabbatical: How a year off reset a media professional - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A 31-year-old media professional took a year off work after experiencing burnout, finding time for personal growth and reconnecting with life outside of work. The break allowed the individual to slow down, prioritize their health, explore new interests, and rediscover passions they had neglected while working.  The experience led them to return to work as a more intentional and grounded professional, prioritizing work-life balance and recognizing that life is not solely defined by career ambitions.

articles.title: M-Audio M Track Duo HD Producer Pack Review: Hot Takes, Cold Opens | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The accessibility of podcasting equipment has made it easier than ever for individuals to start their own shows. M-Audio, a long-standing brand in the budget recording gear market, offers an all-in-one producer pack that provides audio interface, headphones, and a condenser microphone at an affordable price point. This makes starting a podcast accessible to anyone with an idea to share.

articles.title: Scammers Are Using Your Real Hotel Reservations to Trick You With Spear-Phishing Attacks | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Security researchers at Norton have discovered that hundreds of hotels worldwide may have had their customer information stolen in a sophisticated phishing scam. The scam involves cybercriminals using legitimate booking details to create targeted phishing messages, which are designed to trick travelers into revealing sensitive information like credit card details.  The attack appears to be driven by "phishing-as-a-service" software that allows criminals to automate the process of sending and collecting data. While Booking.com and Cloudbeds, a hotel management system provider, have not been breached, the company is working with Europol to investigate the attacks.  Experts warn that hotels need to strengthen security measures to protect customer information from such scams.

articles.title: Ravi Mohan joins the sets of Benz weeks after announcing acting break, see photos | Tamil News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Ravi Mohan, formerly known as Jayam Ravi, has returned to acting after a break following allegations against his estranged wife, Aarti.  He shared the first look of his upcoming film "Benz" with filmmaker Lokesh Kanagaraj, marking his return to the LCU. The production house and celebrity management company The Route also welcomed him to the universe.  Nawaz Javed Kochra, a seasoned entertainment journalist at The Indian Express Online, has been covering the industry for nearly a decade.

articles.title: Arjun Sarja’s Blast shows strong growth at box office, earns Rs 13.18 crore worldwide | Tamil News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Arjun Sarja’s family actioner *Blast* continued its strong performance at the box office over its opening weekend, earning Rs 13.18 crore worldwide. The film saw a significant jump in collections on Day 3, reaching an impressive Rs 7.30 crore net in India.  Directed by Subash K Raj, *Blast* also garnered a global gross of Rs 4.05 crore, contributing to its overall success.  The film stars Arjun Sarja, Abhirami, and Preity Mukhundhan and was released in theaters on May 28th.

articles.title: 7 Best Prepaid Phone Plans (2026) | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Prepaid cellular service offers flexibility and affordability, often using the same networks as major carriers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.  MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) rent network capacity from these companies, offering a range of plans with varying data limits, features, and pricing. While some prepaid services may have restrictions on roaming or international calling, options like US Mobile and Visible offer more comprehensive features at competitive prices. Prepaid plans are generally reliable but can lack domestic roaming in certain areas.  Customers can easily port phone numbers to and from prepaid services, making switching providers a seamless process.

articles.title: Is Premalu 2, sequel to 2024 Malayalam hit, shelved? Actor Naslen breaks silence - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Naslen, the lead actor of the 2024 Malayalam blockbuster "Premalu," confirmed that the sequel, "Premalu 2", has been shelved temporarily due to script issues. articles.title: Quote of the day from Moulin Rouge: ‘The greatest thing you’ll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return’ | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Baz Luhrmann's 2001 film *Moulin Rouge!* continues to resonate with audiences for its enduring message of love and its deeply romantic storytelling. The film stars Ewan McGregor as Christian, an idealistic writer, and Nicole Kidman as Satine, a star performer at the famed Parisian cabaret.  The quote "The greatest thing you’ll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return" delivered by John Leguizamo's Toulouse-Lautrec encapsulates the film's central theme of genuine human connection outweighing wealth, status, and ambition. The film explores the transformative power of love through its protagonists' journeys, highlighting both its joys and challenges.  The quote's enduring appeal lies in its universality, reflecting the profound experience of being loved and reciprocated.

articles.title: 7 dead as car gets crushed between two container trucks in Pune
articles.rephrased_article: Seven people were killed and over a dozen injured in a horrific accident on the Mumbai-Bengaluru Highway in Pune city. A car became trapped between two container trucks that caught fire after one lost control due to a suspected brake failure, according to Deputy Commissioner of Police Sambhaji Kadam.  Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar, who visited the scene, said the fire erupted due to the impact of the collision. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced ₹5 lakh ex-gratia for the families of the deceased.

articles.title: PCI invites claims from eligible Associations of Persons for 15th Term Reconstitution
articles.rephrased_article: The Press Council of India has issued a notice inviting claims from eligible associations managing news agencies for its 15th term. The deadline to submit claims is June 19, 2026, and the process follows Section 5(3)(c) of the Press Council Act, 1978.  The Press Council has also completed its 14th term.

articles.title: Keychron K2 HE Concrete Edition Review: Rock-Solid Typing | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Keychron has released a concrete keyboard, featuring a gray case and standard plastic keycaps. The company's latest product aims to bridge the gap between industrial aesthetics and functional design, offering a well-made and coherent typing experience despite its unconventional material.  The K2 HE keyboard is generating buzz for its unique construction and serves as a conversation starter with its stark appearance.

articles.title: Odisha Gymnastics Apologises After Dead President's Name On Letterhead Sparks Row | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Kumar Sahoo, secretary of the Odisha Gymnastics Association, apologized for continuing to use the late president Samir Dey's name on official letterheads.  Sahoo acknowledged an oversight error and stated that the association is working to rectify it. A complaint has questioned how the OGA secured nearly Rs 98 lakh from the state government for the 2026 National Gymnastics Championships while invoices exceeding Rs 1.96 crore continued to bear Dey's name as president.

articles.title: Aadhaar upgrade soon: Update your mobile number in minutes using new app | Aadhaar Updates | How to change your mobile number
articles.rephrased_article: UIDAI is launching a new app that will allow users to update their mobile numbers without visiting an enrollment center. The update, which costs ₹75 and may take up to 30 days to process, can be accessed through the mAadhaar app on Android and iOS devices. Users must align their face within the app's frame, enter their Aadhaar number and OTP, and verify the new number using facial recognition.

articles.title: No free services for IPL final, clarifies BMRCL - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has denied claims of offering free metro travel for Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) fans on May 31st. The corporation stated that it did not authorize any promotion or advertisement for free travel and urged the public to verify information through official channels, as unauthorized posts and messages are circulating online.

articles.title: Dr Jitendra to inaugurate ‘Lavender festival’ at Bhaderwah on June 6: Director CSIR-IIIM Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State in the PMO, will inaugurate the 4th Lavender festival organized by CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM), Jammu. The festival, themed "Lavender goes global," celebrates the success of lavender cultivation and rural entrepreneurship in J&K.  The event, under the mentorship of Dr Jitendra Singh and guidance of Dr N Kalaiselvi, Director General CSIR and Secretary DSIR, will feature startup exhibitions, live demonstrations, and technical sessions on lavender cultivation and aroma-based products. The festival aims to promote agri-based entrepreneurship, sustainable livelihoods, and innovation in the aromatic crops sector.

articles.title: 550 cancellations and several delays; IndiGo says operations to be normal by February | Onmanorama | India
articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo, the Indian airline, informed the DGCA that it would stabilize its operations by February 10, 2026, following over 550 flight cancellations due to implementation gaps of the new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms. The airline acknowledged misjudgments and planning gaps in implementing the rules, leading to disruptions and a fall in on-time performance. Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu expressed displeasure with the airline's response, while the DGCA will monitor real-time operations and ensure passengers are informed of cancellations well in advance. The airline has sought exemptions from specific FDTL requirements for A320 flights until February 10, 2026, which the DGCA will review.  The DGCA also inspected IndiGo's passenger handling at Delhi airport and instructed the airline to increase manpower and strengthen support services.

articles.title: Many, possibly students, feared trapped as building collapses in Delhi's Saket | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under debris.  The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) responded to the incident and deployed seven fire tenders, while police launched a search and rescue operation. The building housed a coaching institute on the ground floor and construction work was underway on upper floors. Residents are assisting with the rescue efforts, and authorities have not yet confirmed the number of people trapped.

articles.title: Indian citizenship proof: Can you prove your Indian citizenship? I'm not sure I can - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The author reflects on the complexities of proving Indian citizenship, highlighting the lack of a definitive document.  Despite having various documents like identity cards and voter IDs, they are unable to definitively prove their citizenship status. The author compares this situation to God's non-citizen status, emphasizing the ambiguity surrounding citizenship in India. They argue that while there are numerous definitions and documents claiming the opposite, there is no single document proving Indian citizenship. This lack of clarity highlights a frustrating paradox within the Indian legal system.

articles.title: Rabindranath Tagore on happiness and present moment: 'The butterfly counts not months but moments' | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Rabindranath Tagore, a celebrated Bengali writer, poet, and thinker, is known for his philosophy that happiness comes from enjoying each moment rather than focusing on time. Born in 1861, he received the Nobel Prize in Literature and composed national anthems for India and Bangladesh. His works, including poetry collections like "Gitanjali" and novels like "Ghare Baire," have influenced generations of Indians and continue to inspire readers worldwide.  His legacy extends beyond literature, as his music and philosophy remain influential today.

articles.title: Two killed as truck plunges into gorge, catches fire near Gangroo in Ramsoo on NH 44
articles.rephrased_article: A truck carrying limestone caught fire and plunged into a gorge near Gangroo in Ramban district, killing the driver, Shakir Ahmed Manhas, and his conductor, Mohammad Iqbal. The incident occurred on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway early Saturday morning.  Police personnel from Ramsoo police station, volunteers of the Himalayan Quick Response Team (QRT) Ramsoo, CRPF personnel, and Fire and Emergency Services responded to the scene and launched a rescue operation.

articles.title: Ranveer Singh Contacts Farhan Akhtar Amid âDon 3â Controversy, Expresses Interest In Another Film: Report | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ranveer Singh has reached out to Farhan Akhtar to potentially collaborate on a future project, offering to work on another film with him or his sister Zoya Akhtar.  Neither Farhan nor Zoya are currently interested in working with Ranveer again. This follows reports of Ranveer's exit from the film "Don 3" due to creative disagreements and production delays, which led to a legal dispute between Ranveer and Excel Entertainment, Farhan's production company.  Salman Khan reportedly intervened in the conflict, encouraging both sides to prioritize the film industry's interests.

articles.title: Gen Chauhan wraps up 'very satisfying' tenure as CDS; Lt Gen Subramani to take charge Sunday
articles.rephrased_article: Gen Anil Chauhan, the outgoing Chief of Defence Staff, concluded his three-year and eight-month tenure with a ceremonial tri-services guard of honor. He focused on enhancing military synergy among the three services during his time as CDS, playing a key role in Operation Sindoor and the theaterization model. Lt Gen NS Raja Subramani (retd) will succeed him as the next Chief of Defence Staff.  Chauhan expressed gratitude for his tenure and bid farewell to colleagues before transitioning to civilian life.

articles.title: Celina Jaitlyâs Estranged Husband Peter Haag Sends Legal Notices, Seeks Public Apology Over Alleged Defamation | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Celina Jaitly's estranged husband, Peter Haag, and his father, DI Wolfgang J. Haag, have sent legal notices to her demanding a public apology and withdrawal of defamatory statements made against them. The Mumbai-based law firm Semwal & Co. represents the couple and claims that Celina has circulated false allegations through interviews, social media, and media interactions in India and overseas.  The family asserts that these allegations are unsubstantiated and have been used to damage their reputation despite ongoing legal proceedings regarding custody and domestic violence.

articles.title: Five-storey building crashes down in South Delhi's Mehrauli, 10 rescued from debris - Delhi News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket Metro station in South Delhi, triggering a large-scale rescue operation. Delhi Fire Service led the initial response and scaled up operations after confirming the structure's collapse. At least 10 people have been rescued so far, but officials fear several others may still be trapped under the rubble.  Deputy Chief Warden (Headquarters) of Civil Defence Dharamvir Sejwal stated that five to six people are believed to be trapped beneath the debris and that irregularities in the building's construction could have contributed to the collapse. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta expressed concern over the incident and confirmed that all relevant agencies were mobilized, including the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police, Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), and Civil Defence teams. Rescue efforts continue into the night.

articles.title: 5-Storey Building Collapses In South Delhi, Several Feared Trapped
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in south Delhi on Saturday evening, flattening into a massive mound of rubble. Delhi Fire Services received the call at 7:44 pm and sent seven fire tenders to the scene. The building housed a coaching institute on the ground floor and construction work was underway on upper floors, with authorities suspecting students may be trapped. Rescue operations are ongoing as officials try to determine the number of people potentially trapped under the debris.

articles.title: Kelly Curtis, actress and elder sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, dies at 69 | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Kelly Curtis, the elder sister of actress Jamie Lee Curtis, passed away at age 69 on Saturday.  She was a talented actress who appeared in films like "Trading Places" and "The Devil's Daughter," as well as television series such as "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine."  Curtis is survived by her husband, playwright Scott Morfee.  Tributes have poured in from colleagues, fans, and members of the entertainment industry.

articles.title: Best road trips near Mumbai to take this June for misty hills, beaches, and quick escapes | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mumbai residents seeking a monsoon escape can consider several road trip options within driving distance. Lonavala, known for its waterfalls and misty views, is a popular choice for spontaneous weekend breaks.  Matheran, India's only automobile-free hill station, offers peaceful retreats with red mud trails and scenic viewpoints. Alibaug provides coastal drives, beaches, and relaxed vacation energy, while Igatpuri boasts lush landscapes and dramatic valley views. Nashik offers vineyard getaways, temple visits, and local food.  For those willing to travel further, the Satara belt presents waterfalls, ghats, and scenic roads.

articles.title: Salman Khan Only Owns One Rolex—But His Real Collection Is Worth Crores
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Khan has a significant watch collection, including a Rolex Rainbow Daytona valued at ₹5.13 crore and a Jacob & Co. "Ram Janmabhoomi" timepiece gifted by his mother. He collaborated with Jacob & Co. to create the "Billionaire III," featuring 714 diamonds, which is a tribute to his father's legacy. The actor has showcased various watches over the years, including a limited-edition "Epic X Ram Janmabhoomi Titanium Edition 2" from Jacob & Co., valued at ₹34 lakhs.

articles.title: Obsession takeover: A Rs 7 crore horror film just exposed Bollywood’s biggest issue - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A low-budget horror film, "Obsession," directed by Curry Barker and starring Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, has become Hollywood's biggest ROI story of 2026.  The film, made for a reported budget of $750,000 to $1 million (roughly Rs 6–8 crore), grossed over $100 million worldwide, earning nearly 80 to 100 times its production cost. This success highlights the shrinking space for mid-budget theatrical films in Bollywood, where studios increasingly prioritize large-scale spectacles and franchise universes.  The film's low-risk, high-concept storytelling model contrasts with the escalating budgets of recent blockbuster releases like "RRR" and "Dhurandhar: The Revenge," which have also achieved significant box office success but rely on massive production costs.

articles.title: Three boys drown in tank in Dharwad taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three boys, aged 11, 13, and 15, drowned in a village tank in Dharwad taluk on Saturday while swimming. Police Superintendent Gunjan Arya, Deputy Superintendent of Police Vinod Muktedar, and other officials responded to the scene and recovered the bodies with assistance from expert swimmers.

articles.title: The poet who shaped a filmmaker: Vishal Bhardwaj recalls a lifetime of friendship with Bashir Badr
articles.rephrased_article: Vishal Bhardwaj, a renowned filmmaker, mourns the passing of Bashir Badr, a celebrated Urdu poet.  Badr, who died at 91, was known for his profound impact on Bhardwaj's life and career. The two shared a deep bond that began in Meerut, where Bhardwaj was a student and Badr taught. Their friendship spanned decades, during which Bhardwaj learned from Badr's poetry and became a successful filmmaker.  Bhardwaj has honored Badr through his work, including incorporating his poems into films like "Dedh Ishqiya" and composing ghazals based on Badr's verses.  The two remained close even as Bhardwaj's career flourished in Mumbai, with Badr visiting him often and offering encouragement.

articles.title: Naga Chaitanya Approaches Delhi HC Over Defamatory Content Alleging He Cheated On Samantha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Naga Chaitanya, an actor, has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against online content and defamatory claims alleging he cheated on his ex-wife Samantha Ruth Prabhu. The actor's legal team argues that unauthorized use of his name, image, and persona across various platforms is damaging his reputation.  Justice Jyoti Singh acknowledged the vulnerability of public figures but stressed limitations to scrutiny. The court will examine Chaitanya's plea for legal protections against such online misuse.

articles.title: Indian student drowned at Wisconsin dam as he jumped to save three friends; feet got stuck in fishing wire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anurup Reddy Koduru, a 22-year-old Indian student who recently graduated from the University of North Texas, drowned at Toledo Bend Reservoir on May 29th.  He was swimming with friends when he became entangled in fishing wire and was pulled under water. The incident involved multiple agencies including the South Sabine Fire District, LA Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, North Sabine Fire District, Sabine River Authority, Acadian Ambulance, Life Air Rescue, and the Sabine Parish Sheriff Dive Team. Ashtrith Reddy Koduru, his brother, has set up a fundraiser to help with repatriation and funeral expenses.

articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed in south Delhi's Mehrauli area on Saturday evening, trapping dozens of people under the debris. Delhi Fire Service personnel responded quickly, calling for reinforcements and cordoning off the area to facilitate rescue efforts.

articles.title: Salary denied for more than 2 years, Olympian judge Bilquis Mir moves CAT
articles.rephrased_article: Bilquis Mir, an Olympian judge and high-profile sports administrator, has filed a contempt case against the Jammu and Kashmir sports department for withholding her salary for over two years.  Mir's legal battle stems from a February order by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) directing the release of her salary. Despite this, the J-K government has failed to comply with the court's directive, leading to Mir seeking further action through the CAT and High Court. The case highlights the ongoing financial and professional challenges faced by Mir due to bureaucratic delays and raises concerns about the treatment of talented athletes in the region.

articles.title: Building collapses near Saket metro station; 8 persons rescued, several feared trapped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An eight-story building collapsed in Saket, Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under the debris. Delhi Fire Services officials responded to the scene and rescued at least eight individuals.  The incident occurred near a tin shed canteen where children were dining, creating panic and prompting a large-scale rescue operation involving multiple agencies including National Disaster Response Force, Delhi Police, and District Disaster Management Authority.

articles.title: Kochi metro worksite accident: SHRC registers suo motu case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) Chairperson Alexander Thomas has requested an investigation by the Ernakulam District Collector into a car accident involving a woman who sustained injuries from an iron piece falling at a Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) worksite. The Commission seeks information on the incident's cause, the woman's injuries, vehicle damage, compensation status, and KMRL and its contractor's safety measures.  The Collector is expected to submit a report within three weeks, with the Commission requiring both the Managing Director of KMRL and a senior officer representing them to present at a subsequent hearing on July 14th.

articles.title: India’s scientific knowledge predates Persia, brought West out of Stone Age: Jammu and Kashmir Lt. Governor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jammu & Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha stated that India's knowledge in science, medicine, and astronomy predates Persia and Western countries. He emphasized India's historical role as a center of knowledge for centuries, contributing to global civilization and culture.  Sinha highlighted the Vedic period as a foundation for socio-economic advancement across the world.

articles.title: Youth must believe in their potential, says Sharanbasappa Pappa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharanbasappa Pappa, president of the Kalyana Karnataka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KKCCI), encouraged youth in the region to cultivate self-confidence and determination for success.  He praised the initiative of Adhish Wali, president of the Rotary Club Bidar Silverstar, who organized the two-day Rise Kalyana Karnataka- an Educational Youth Summit 2026. The summit featured a Mega Job Fair with over 50 companies, attracting more than 1,500 students and job aspirants.  Tejasvi Surya, MP for Bengaluru South, delivered a virtual address, alongside entrepreneurs Karan Javali, Swathi Kulkarni, and Anilkumar Bidve.

articles.title: Marcia Lucas: Oscar-winning Star Wars editor dies aged 80
articles.rephrased_article: Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning editor of the original Star Wars film, has died at 80 from metastatic cancer.  She was married to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, and worked on several of his films including *THX 1138* and *American Graffiti*.  Lucas won an Academy Award for Best Film Editing in 1977 for *A New Hope*, and also collaborated with directors like Martin Scorsese on acclaimed films. Her family described her as a "trailblazer" who helped redefine film editing, leaving behind a legacy of emotional intelligence and impactful storytelling.
